title: Concourse: first look

claims.text: Concourse is an AI execution layer for enterprise finance teams, which matches Accel's AI focus.
Concourse is at Series A, which sits within Accel's seed to late-stage range.
The company is US-based, which is within Accel's Americas coverage.
Concourse says it works with 100+ finance departments, a sign of early customer traction.
The company reports 75% reduction in manual work and 20+ hours saved per team member for customers.
Accel's listed portfolio shows AI as one of its most represented sectors.
The company is very small, with approximately seven employees according to one profile.
The company's own website makes performance claims, such as 86% reduction in manual finance work, that are not independently verified in the sources.
Funding details are missing: no amount, date or lead investor is recorded in the dataset.
Crunchbase and other profiles describe the company only briefly and do not confirm funding history.
Concourse's own site describes heavy services work, including white-glove deployment and custom builds, which may limit how scalable the software is.

questions: What is the size and lead investor of the Series A, and is the company raising now?
How much of revenue comes from software subscriptions versus custom services and deployment work?
What are the verified customer retention rates and the basis for the 75% and 86% efficiency claims?
What is the team's background and how many people will be hired with the new capital?
How does the company differentiate from larger finance software vendors and AI-native competitors?

trust.disclaimer: Public sources only. Not investment advice.
